rationale: Measured human CSF exposure: 77.7 nM mean (range 5.7-288.5), detected in 9 of 12 paediatric brain tumour patients (PMID 32493453). The rodent brain:plasma fraction of 3-7% is not opposing evidence - the same mouse study's absolute figures are 394 nM in brain against 11.6 uM in plasma, so a low fraction of a high plasma level still gives a substantial brain concentration. Carries no claim about whether 78 nM engages any particular target; the pipeline holds no target-engagement threshold.

Both human CSF studies measure the same concentration, about 1 nM: PMID 42578491 reports 0.5 +/- 0.2 ng/mL (1.02 nM) against plasma 101.6 ng/mL, a 225:1 plasma:CSF ratio, and PMID 32493453 reports a mean of 1.2 nM. The second reads as supporting only because 1.2 nM sits at the floor of its 1-10 nM 'moderate' bucket. A third clinical report (PMID 24790822) could not detect dasatinib in CSF above a 1 ng/mL threshold at 40 mg daily, and mouse brain:plasma is under 0.12. No empirical disagreement exists between the two sides - only the adjectives differ. Caveat: dasatinib's potency is itself low-nanomolar, so ~1 nM is not self-evidently sub-therapeutic for every target; the pipeline holds no target-engagement threshold.

All three studies agree pazopanib reaches only a minority fraction of plasma levels, but they differ about sevenfold on how small. PMID 22749591 (dedicated bioanalytical PK) gives brain:plasma AUC 0.015; PMID 22688250 reports distribution 'severely limited due to active efflux', rescued ~5-fold only by dual P-gp/Bcrp1 inhibition. PMID 28869476 (Javidnia 2017, supplied by Kara) reports brain Cmax 450 ng/mL at 5 mg/kg and 583 ng/mL at 10 mg/kg; its Fig 1B serum values, read off the chart at the 4 h Tmax, are roughly 4,000 and 6,500 ng/mL, giving brain:serum of 11% and 9% (AUC ratio 0.11-0.12). That study dosed intraperitoneally rather than orally and did NOT perfuse its PK animals - perfusion is described only for histology - so residual vascular blood plausibly inflates its brain figure. Recorded as contradicted on direction, with the 7-fold spread and the ~1 uM absolute brain concentration (above pazopanib's target IC50s) noted as unresolved.
